Our Values
Kind Hearts
Kind Hearts
We foster a culture of kindness, empathy, and respect, where everyone feels safe, valued, and supported to flourish. As a listening school, we prioritise mutual respect, oracy, and emotional wellbeing, helping pupils thrive socially, emotionally, and academically. Our commitment extends beyond school through charitable initiatives and community partnerships, encouraging pupils to care for others and make a positive difference.
Curious Minds
Curious Minds
We celebrate curiosity as the spark for lifelong learning, encouraging pupils to ask questions, think critically, and explore beyond the classroom. Through academic rigour, creativity, and a wide range of opportunities, we nurture independent, imaginative thinkers with the confidence to adapt, innovate, and grow with a global perspective.
Courageous Futures
Courageous Futures
We empower pupils to face challenges with confidence, resilience, and integrity. Encouraging bold ideas and brave decisions, we help them persevere, adapt, and grow stronger. Rooted in our pioneering heritage, we champion co-education, diversity and inclusion, preparing young people to shape a kinder, and more sustainable world.
At Ibstock, we believe in nurturing kind hearts, inspiring curious minds, and guiding courageous futures.
These values shape everything we do — from how we support each pupil’s personal growth to the way we create a dynamic learning environment and prepare them for life beyond school.

Together, these values guide us in shaping compassionate, confident learners who are ready to embrace their future with heart, mind, and courage.

About us
With an urban location and a beautiful botanical feel, Ibstock is the perfect home for scholarly exploration and adventure.
Ibstock Place School is a co-educational day school for pupils aged 3 to 18, set within a beautiful eight-acre campus on the edge of Richmond Park. Championing co-education since its founding in 1894, Ibstock embodies the best of modern education: academically ambitious, emotionally intelligent and socially conscious. At Ibstock, we believe schools should be places of joy. Childhood is precious, and our pupils flourish in an environment that is both challenging and supportive, ambitious and kind.

Prep 4 Exploring Shapes and Space in Mathematics
Investigating Tessellations and 3D Geometry Through Practical Learning.
In Mathematics, pupils explored tessellations by investigating how different shapes fit together to create repeating patterns without gaps or overlaps. They also used a variety of practical resources to build and examine 3D shapes, developing their understanding of faces, edges, and vertices through engaging hands-on activities.

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion
Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI)
Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) are embedded in Ibstock's curriculum design, pastoral provision and whole-school culture to ensure that our pupils experience it as a lived reality throughout their education.
To ensure everyone can thrive and meet their full potential, inclusion and equality is at the core of our ethos, aligning with our school values of Kind Hearts, Curious Minds, and Courageous Futures.
We proactively foster social cohesion in all areas of school life, pastoral, academic and co-curricular, and seek to remove any barriers to access, participation, progression, attainment, and achievement. We will not tolerate any form of discrimination. You can read our Equality, Diversity and inclusion policy in full here.
Clubs and Societies
A range of co-curricular clubs and societies support our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion work including:
Celebrations
Beyond the classroom, EDI at Ibstock is made visible and meaningful through a whole-school programme of commemorative events and action-based initiatives.
Through celebrations including PRIDE, International Women's Day, Black History Month, Neurodiversity Week and Period Power Day, we show support not only to individual pupils who feel themselves celebrated, but also to their friends and colleagues whose understanding and knowledge is broadened.
Pupil Voice
Pupil Voice is strong at Ibstock, with significant representation from EDI voices in our Sixth Form Cabinet including Race and Heritage Reps, LGBTQ Reps and Gender Equality Reps, who work with the Director of EDI and lead societies.
Our pupils also benefit from listening to other voices by working with outside providers in workshops including Beyond Equality, Bold Voices and ACEN (African and Caribbean Education Network).
Our Curriculum
At Ibstock, our distinctive Compass Learning philosophy places every learner at the heart of their educational experience. Through the 'Unique Journeys' pillar, we recognise that each pupil brings their own strengths, experiences and perspectives. This commitment shapes an inclusive approach to teaching and learning, where curriculum access, representation and aspiration are tailored to the needs and identities of every individual—not a one-size-fits-all model.
Our Pathways (PSHE) curriculum provides a structured, progressive framework for developing pupils' understanding of equality, diversity and inclusion. Using a spiral curriculum, pupils revisit key themes throughout their school journey, deepening their knowledge, emotional literacy and critical thinking over time. Through exploring topics such as identity, discrimination, gender, sexuality, relationships, democracy and equality, they learn to engage thoughtfully with complex social issues and develop genuine respect for others. Learning is grounded in real-world contexts and lived experiences, encouraging pupils to challenge stereotypes, recognise structural inequality, and communicate with empathy, confidence and respect.
Through our Futures (Careers) programme, we work to widen opportunity and raise aspirations. Pupils gain insight into a broad range of careers, pathways and the changing world of work through up-to-date labour market information and meaningful careers education. We actively challenge gender stereotypes and other barriers to aspiration, while encouraging pupils to reflect on how factors such as background, circumstance and privilege can influence access to opportunities. By developing an awareness of both their own experiences and those of others, pupils are equipped to recognise inequality, value fairness and make informed, socially responsible choices about their futures. In this way, Ibstock's commitment to EDI extends beyond identity and culture to encompass access, opportunity and social mobility.

Partnerships & Community | Ibstock Place School, Roehampton | Private Prep School Near Richmond, Barnes, Putney, Kingston, & Wandsworth
Partnerships and Community
With our London location, we are proud to be part of such a diverse and inclusive local community and to make a significant contribution to it.
We continue to grow our extensive partnerships programme in which our pupils play a leading part, and to deepen existing relationships with local community groups. A complete record of our partnership activities may be found via the Independent Schools’ Council and its Schools Together website.
Download our Partnership and Community Brochure
Matched Funding Initiative
Matched Funding Initiative
Our incredible FIPS (Families of Ibstock Place School) continue to run the wonderful Matched Funding Initiative.
Ibstock pupils can apply to have any fundraising they undertake matched to the value of £500. Pupils have raised money for charities including the RNLI, Walk The Walk (breast cancer charity), The Kids Cancer Charity, and the Royal Parks Charity.
Fundraising for Refugees: The Big House Read
Fundraising for Refugees: The Big House Read
In the face of the appalling tragedies that force people to flee their homes due to conflict, natural disasters, or fear of persecution, we wanted to do something positive.
We are reading for good. Schools and individuals across the UK, supported by the School Library Association (SLA), have been reading as if their lives depend on it (because, in many cases, lives truly do depend on it) to raise money for refugees around the world.
Organised by our inspirational librarian, Helen Cleaves, our pupils have been taking part in sponsored reading to raise money for the charity UNHCR, which protects refugees worldwide by providing life-saving emergency assistance.
We are also proud that two of our pupils hand-painted a design that was used nationwide on campaign posters.
Lower Sixth Form Leadership and Volunteering
Lower Sixth Form Leadership and Volunteering
We are particularly proud of our Lower Sixth Formers and their contributions to community projects outside of School.
All Lower Sixth pupils who continue with three A-levels rather than four begin a weekly, timetabled volunteering project in November, which runs for the remainder of the academic year. Recent projects include reading and providing lesson support at nearby Alton, Heathmere, Sheen Mount and Mosaic Jewish Primary Schools; supporting pupils with special educational needs at Paddock, Linden Lodge School and Roehampton Gate School; improving neglected green spaces on the Alton Estate; and supporting intergenerational activities in Roehampton with Charity Sparkle Together. Each year, around 70 Lower Sixth pupils take part in this wonderful scheme.
YungMash Collective Fashion Show
YungMash Collective Fashion Show
The Wall (our award-winning pupil-led magazine) holds a special annual Fashion Show to raise money for the YungMash Collective.
Established by our former Head Girl, Masha Shishkina, the Collective supports young adults in peer-to-peer mentoring relationships.
Rackets Cubed Partnership and Fundraising
Rackets Cubed Partnership and Fundraising
Charity Rackets Cubed works nationally to enhance "the long-term achievement of inner-City kids through integrated Sports, Education and Nutrition programmes".
It organises weekly extra-curricular racket sports activities, as well as maths support sessions, which are rounded off with a healthy meal. In addition to being a host site for these sessions, Ibstock pupils have been helping the younger pupils who attend from one of our local partner schools.
The Ibstock community also holds regular donation drives to provide essential items, which are delivered by the charity to those who need them most. We are committed to strengthening this long-term partnership.
Intergenerational Tea Party for Elderly Roehampton Residents
Intergenerational Tea Party
A group of 30 Senior 10 pupils used their own initiative to plan and host a tea party for local elderly residents in Roehampton.
A raffle, quiz, concert, and delicious refreshments provided by Ibstock’s catering team made for a truly enjoyable event. It was clear that both young and old gained a great deal from interacting with one another and sharing their experiences. For many guests, getting out and socialising can be a struggle, so this occasion helped to facilitate that. We hope to make this a regular community event.
Sustainability
At Ibstock, sustainability is woven into every aspect of our community. Guided by a clear vision to reach carbon net zero, we are committed to protecting biodiversity, reducing waste, and promoting clean energy while inspiring our pupils to become responsible stewards of the planet. From our “Meat Free Mondays” to tree planting, cycling initiatives, and hands-on projects in our gardens, we encourage a deep connection with nature. By embedding sustainability across our teaching, operations, and daily choices, we are empowering pupils to lead with compassion and innovation in a rapidly changing world. Careers & HE Support | Ibstock Place Sixth Form, Roehampton | Private Prep School Near Richmond, Barnes, Putney, Kingston, & Wandsworth
Careers and Higher Education Support
Making decisions about the future can be daunting. At Ibstock all of our pupils benefit from an extensive Careers and Higher Education programme.
We also ensure that they are provided with Careers Guidance right from the start of their Senior School journey so that as they are presented with options further up the school, they can make informed decisions.
Higher Education Support
All of our pupils are actively encouraged to enrich their Higher Education application through their participation in essay competitions and taster courses while, of course, we maintain strong links with our past pupils who can offer their successors up-to-date knowledge of life across the UK’s many campuses.
With over 80% of pupils typically attaining offers from Russell Group institutions, we have an extensive pool of experience on which to draw, and popular Ibstock Leavers’ destinations include the likes of Oxford and Cambridge, Birmingham, Bristol, Durham, Exeter, Imperial College London, Lancaster, Leeds, Liverpool, LSE, Queen Mary, London, Nottingham, Sussex, UCL and Warwick. Click here to see our university destinations map.
Early Application Support Team
Our Early Applications Support Team is led by our Deputy Head of Sixth Form (Academic) and brings together expert teachers in their chosen field, many of which have firsthand experience working in a Higher Education environment.
EAST supports pupils looking to apply to Oxford, Cambridge or other UK courses which require an earlier application submission such as Medicine, Veterinary Science and Dentistry. The EAST Programme officially starts in Senior 11 with pupils attending lectures and sessions which offer a taste of what makes a competitive application.
In the Lower Sixth, pupils in EAST meet on a weekly basis and work on the mechanics of their application as well as looking at skills required as part of the assessment process for these courses or institutions. Pupils in EAST who also require specialist assistance in preparing their application, are allocated a ‘subject mentor’ who helps review their wider reading and preparation for any entrance tests required.
This support continues into the Upper Sixth with extra input from ‘subject mentors’ on preparation for interviews and entrance tests. As part of EAST pupils also take part in a series of mock interviews conducted by subject specialists from outside the School community.
International University Admissions
We have a designated member of staff on the Sixth Form Tutor Team who is responsible for admissions to institutions of higher education outside of the United Kingdom. We have seen an increase in interest from our pupils in applying to such institutions, particularly in Europe and the United States of America.
We host an annual International Universities Fair which pupils from Senior 7 are welcome to attend to ask any questions and to find out about the opportunities to study abroad. We also offer support to our families through meetings and presentations so that they are aware of the possibilities of international study and how to support their children with an application.
Careers Support
Sixth Form builds on the considerable Careers support pupils receive throughout Senior School.
A combination of tutorial time, one-to-one meetings, work experience, events and visiting speakers, help pupils to explore a range of career paths and build knowledge and experience to inform their next steps post School or University.
Annual Careers Fair
Our Annual Careers Fair takes place every Spring Term and affords pupils in Senior 10 to Lower Sixth the opportunity to hear from over 20 professionals from a wide range of fields about their careers to date. Each pupil picks three sessions to attend, based on their interests and ambitions.

Specialist Teaching | Ibstock Place Pre-Prep School, Roehampton | Private Prep School Near Richmond, Barnes, Putney, Kingston, & Wandsworth
Creative Arts
From Kindergarten, our pupils enjoy dedicated Art, Design & Technology, Music and Creative Arts taught by specialist staff.
Art & Design
Art and Design & Technology are generously timetabled and taught in a dedicated Art studio.
From Kindergarten, pupils have ownership of their creative space and feel comfortable moving around the studio with confidence and independence.
Ibstock has an exciting, ambitious and broad Art curriculum. Pupils are encouraged to view their Art lessons beyond the learning of technical skills as the process of looking; organising; thinking; wondering; questioning; imagining; communicating and enjoyment.
Design & Technology involves two important elements: learning about how things work and learning to design and make functional products for particular purposes and users. Children have the opportunity to tackle problems of a practical nature which equips them with important life skills.
In the Summer term we hold an Arts Week, sparking our pupils’ creativity through a wide range of artist-led workshops centred around an annual theme. The week ends with a highly anticipated Arts Show, exhibiting the work of our talented pupils to family and friends. Take a look at last year’s ‘Under the Sea’ theme.
Music & Creative Arts
Pupils enjoy creating, performing and evaluating music across a range of historical periods, genres and traditions.
Through our dedicated team of over 15 visiting music teachers, pupils can learn an array of instruments.
Outside of the classroom there are lots of ways for pupils to get involved in music, from String Ensembles to the Big Sing, and Rock Bands to Ukulele Singer-Songwriters.
Building performance experience is crucial not only for musicians, but for all children in developing their confidence and resilience. There are a range of performance opportunities, including our ‘ Tea-Time Concert’ series, giving young musicians the experience of playing to a small and friendly audience of parents and other performers.
Watch our pupils marching as part of the Grow Roehampton Street Band. Performing as part of Wandsworth Arts Festival, bringing the local community together and having fun through music.

Expressive Arts | Ibstock Place Prep School, Roehampton | Private Prep School Near Richmond, Barnes, Putney, Kingston, & Wandsworth
Expressive Arts
The ability to think and express creatively contributes enormously to the development of the whole child: emotionally, aesthetically, physically, socially and cognitively.
We want to ignite our pupils’ imagination, give them the confidence to express themselves and to better understand the world around them.
At Ibstock, Expressive Arts are embedded into the Curriculum with many further Co-Curricular options also available. Whilst there is much collaboration between all the Arts, we divide them into three departments: Art and Design & Technology, Music and Creative Arts.
Art and Design & Technology
Pupils are encouraged to view their Art and Design & Technology lessons beyond the learning of technical skills as the process of looking; organising; thinking; wondering; questioning; imagining; communicating and enjoyment.
Art lessons provide all children with the opportunity to express themselves imaginatively, creatively and develops their understanding of the world around them. Pupils are exposed to many sensory experiences whilst exploring a vast range of media, artists and cultures.
Design and Technology involves two important elements: learning about the design world and how things work and learning to design and make functional products for purposes and users. Children work independently and in groups, learning to co-operate, plan, design and make and evaluate their work.
Timetable
Art and Design & Technology are generously timetabled and taught in a dedicated Art studio. The terms are split into the following directive teaching across the whole Pre-Prep & Prep School.
Autumn Term: Fine Art
Spring Term: Design & Technology
Music
We offer a wide-ranging programme of musical education for all pupils, from the beginner to the most advanced performer. We aim to foster a love and enjoyment of music and performing and to make music accessible to all pupils.
In the early years, children build listening and performing skills through singing, movement, and percussion. We introduce a wide range of styles, inspiring imagination and the first steps in composition. From Prep 3, pupils progress to reading notation, recognising form and harmony, and performing in parts with confidence. They compose using drones, chords, and contrasting sections, while broadening their appreciation of music from Coleridge-Taylor and Beethoven to Jazz, World, and Contemporary styles. By Prep 6, our pupils perform expressively in ensembles and celebrate their achievements in the end-of-year production.
All pupils receive one hour of Music tution a week. Lessons are centred around physically exploring music through movement, as well as exploring sound through listening, composing, improvising and performing.
Developing singing voices and instrumental skills as a class, helps our pupils develop self-esteem, communication skills, expressiveness and creativity.
Our musicians are encouraged to practice their performance skills just as much as their instruments and voices, so we provide as many opportunities as possible to gain experience in front of an audience. Platforms range from Assemblies, Teatime Concerts, Autumn and Summer Concerts, to special events like the Carol Service and the Roehampton Community Street Band.
Co-Curricular Music Activities
Live performance is a vital part of life in the Music department and pupils regularly have the opportunity to perform as soloists and in ensembles. Our extensive Ensembles provision reflects a broad range of musical tastes and styles and is designed to cater to as many interests and abilities as possible. Our ensembles include:
Chamber Choir (Prep 3-6)
Chamber Choir (Prep 5 & 6, audition only)
Lower Prep Choir (Prep 2 & 3)
Music Technology Club
Ukulele/Singer Songwriter Group
Instrumental Lessons:
Pupils are able to take instrumental lessons with our Visiting Music Teachers from Prep 1. Instrumental lessons take place during the school day and are scheduled on a rotating basis, minimising the impact on time away from the curriculum. All of our visiting music teachers are experienced, talented musicians, with specialist skills in teaching young people. Pupils have a wide range of instruments to choose from as they progress through the Prep School and every instrument has a corresponding Ensemble to further enhance pupil progress.
String Scheme and Recorder Scheme:
We are proud to run two instrumental schemes, designed to give pupils a flavour of what it might be like to learn an instrument. All pupils in Prep 1 receive a term of tuition from our professional visiting music teachers on either the violin or cello, before being offered the chance to continue as part of the String Scheme, which offers small ensemble sessions to compliment the work undertaken in private lessons. Similarly, all pupils in Prep 3 are offered the chance to learn the recorder, getting to grips with the basics for a term. Even if children choose not to continue the instrumental tuition, understanding the commitment and discipline required to learn an instrument is an important part of appreciating music.
Creative Arts
All pupils receive one hour a week of Creative Arts, which includes Dance and Drama. Every lesson is practical and collaborative, enabling pupils to develop their transferrable skills including communication, teamwork, and leadership.
Pupils are taught the skills needed for choreographing dance and devising drama, encouraging them to think creatively.
Specialist Dance lessons where pupils can concentrate on a particular style, are part of our Co-Curricular offering.
Pupils are also taught Performing Skills for a variety of styles and genres to help in preparation for Showcases and Plays.

Prep School Art Week 2026 | News | Ibstock Place School, Roehampton | Private School Near Richmond, Barnes, Putney, Kingston, & Wandsworth
Prep School Art Week 2026
Our Prep School celebrated a fantastic Arts Week, with this year’s inspiring theme: Architecture.
From Kindergarten to Prep 6, pupils explored a variety of artistic media, unleashing their creativity to produce an impressive range of artwork, structures, and designs. Throughout the week, each class took part in workshops led by local artists, resulting in a remarkable collection of architectural creations.
The exhibition featured an exciting array of structures, including the British Museum, geodesic domes, domed cathedrals, castles, Roman bridges, cityscapes, and much more. As well as developing their artistic skills, pupils gained valuable insight into the engineering principles behind these iconic structures and discovered the important role engineering plays in architecture and design.
A huge thank you the Art Department and visiting artists whose enthusiasm, expertise, and hard work helped make the Arts Week exhibition such a memorable and inspiring success.

pageCache.text:
Expressive Arts | Ibstock Place Senior School, Roehampton | Private School Near Richmond, Barnes, Putney, Kingston, & Wandsworth
Expressive Arts
Expressive Arts play a vital role in the life of the School. Aside from bringing enjoyment and fostering numerous transferable skills, the ability to think and express creatively is ever more fundamental to a whole range of career paths.
At Ibstock we offer a wide variety of inclusive and exclusive opportunities to allow every pupil, regardless of age or ability, to discover and develop their creative talent or passion.
There is a full programme of termly concerts, shows, and productions, in addition to many low-stakes, day-to-day performance opportunities.
Music
Music is a hugely important part of the curriculum here at Ibstock, from Kindergarten through to the Sixth Form.
Whether it’s classical, rock and pop, or musical theatre, all styles are equally celebrated and nurtured.
In addition to our beautiful Ballroom and state-of-the-art Theatre, the school is exceptionally well-equipped. We have three purpose-built music classrooms with specialist recording facilities, and twelve dedicated practice rooms - including our unique soundproof Armadilla Pods.
Our musicians are encouraged to develop not only their technical skills, but also their confidence as performers. We offer a wealth of opportunities to take to the stage - through assemblies, recitals, evensongs, seasonal concerts, termly ensemble concerts, and major events like the Carol Service and annual Prize Giving.
Highlights of the musical year include international tours, our prestigious Ibstock in Concert at Sinfonia Smith Square, performances in major cathedrals - including our annual service at St Paul’s Cathedral - and two hotly contested competitions: Classical Musician of the Year and Popular Musician of the Year. Our entirely pupil-led House Music Competition is also a standout event that captures the spirit, leadership, and creativity of our students.
Music Ensembles and Clubs
Individual Music Lessons
The benefits of learning a musical instrument are well documented. There has been much research to show that music lessons have a disproportionately positive impact on academic attainment.
Several hundred pupils take instrumental lessons on a large selection of instruments, including Violin, viola, cello, double-bass, harp, flute, clarinet, saxophone, bassoon, oboe, recorder, trumpet, French horn, trombone, euphonium, guitar, bass guitar, organ, piano, jazz piano, percussion and voice.
We also offer both classical and contemporary singing lessons.
We enter pupils termly for ABRSM and Trinity graded music examinations termly and pupils can also be entered for Rock School and LCME qualifications. For further information, please click here. If you would like to sign your child up for music lessons, please fill in this form.
Music Tours and Trips
This year the Ibstock Place School Choir will heading off to Bath and Wells, Somerset, but in recent years they have enjoyed successful tours to Venice and Verona, Budapest, and Umbria.
In September, the school's top ensembles perform at our annual large-scale choral and orchestral concert, Ibstock in Concert, at a central London venue. The venue for 2026 is St Gabriel's, Pimlico; in previous years, the venue has been Sinfonia, Smith Square.
The Berkley Ensemble, Ibstock Ensemble in Residence
Hailed as ‘an instinctive collective’ (The Strad), the Berkeley Ensemble was formed in 2008 by members of Southbank Sinfonia, Britain’s young professional orchestra, with the aim of exploring the wealth of little-known twentieth- and twenty-first century British chamber music alongside more established repertoire. It now enjoys a busy concert schedule performing throughout the UK and abroad and is also much in demand for its inspiring work in education.
We are delighted that the Berkeley Ensemble’s association with Ibstock Place School includes:
We collaborate with Wandsworth Music Hub and regularly host music examinations for external candidates. National Youth Music Theatre has also used our facilities as rehearsal spaces. Masterclasses have also taken place at Ibstock as part of Barnes Music Festival. We also have an annual Ibstock Brass Day for local primary schools, in collaboration with Wandsworth Music Hub and Friary Brass Band.
We run an annual singing day in the Summer Term for pupils from local primary school.
Ibstock musicians also regularly perform to groups and in venues in our local community.

Drama
The Drama Department organises a tremendous range of activities and opportunities.
In a typical calendar year we host Lower and Upper Senior productions, a Senior 10 production, an annual Theatre Company production (for Drama Scholars), termly LAMDA showcases, and a House Drama competition which sees pupils write, produce, and perform their own plays.
'We offer outstanding opportunities for pupils, whether centre stage or behind the scenes.'
Recent productions have included Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, Footloose, and We Will Rock You. Calendar year 2025/26 saw sell-out productions of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang (Lower Senior Production) and While the Lights Were Out (Upper Senior Production). Ibstock pupils regularly take up places as members of the National Youth Theatre and National Youth Music Theatre, and many past pupils have gone on to train at leading Drama schools such as RADA, LAMDA, Mountview, Rose Bruford, and secured careers in Theatre and film. Alongside renowned institutions like E15 and NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts, our alumni have gone on to achieve great success — with former pupils now performing in the West End, including the exciting new Hunger Games production.
To enrich the GCSE and A Level course, we invite practitioners in to run specific workshops. We have been lucky to learn directly from Frantic Assembly, the Stanislavski Experience and Paper Birds. Previous visitors have been Matt Henry (Laurence Olivier Award Winner and OBE), Michael Oakley (Theatre Director) Nicola Sanderson (Actor) and Ben Westerby (Actor and Ibstock Alumni).
Trips are arranged throughout the year to a range of theatres in Richmond, Hammersmith, Kingston and the West End to enable our pupils to see a range of spaces and styles. Previous productions include: The Woman in Black, The Hound of the Baskervilles, The Play that Goes Wrong, Metamorphosis, Othello, As You Like It, Medea, Accidental Death of an Anarchist, Witness for the Prosecution and Little Big Things.
London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA)
LAMDA lessons and examinations are exceptionally popular across the entire pupil body with stellar results to match.
As the oldest and one of the most prestigious drama schools in the country, we are incredibly proud of the large number of pupils from Prep 3 upwards, who take classes with our specialist teachers.
For further information, please click here. If you would like to sign your child up for LAMDA lessons, please fill in this form.
Facilities
Our magnificent main theatre comprises a stage, auditorium, and gallery with seating for up to 250.
Facilities include an orchestra pit, extensive foyer areas, green room and dressing rooms. With two further studio theatres and two full-time theatre technicians, we offer outstanding opportunities for pupils, whether centre stage or behind the scenes.
In the most recent examinations 86% of pupils achieved distinctions.
All examinations support pupils to develop a broad range of skills and knowledge, not only in performance but also speaking in public, development of language skills, appreciation of literature and working as part of a team.
Dance
Dance is very popular, with an increasing number of styles on offer and lessons run by specialist teachers.
A highlight of the annual Dance calendar is our whole school Dance Show, providing a chance to showcase a variety of dance techniques and choreography, bringing all ages together.
In addition to co-curricular lessons, pupils enjoy workshops from visiting companies such as the National Youth Dance Company (NYDC) and trips.
We offer a wide range of co-curricular classes for all year groups before/after school and at lunchtime on Monday to Friday each week.
Pupils have the option of taking private/semi- private lessons in preparation for Dance Exams including Royal Academy of Dance Ballet (RAD), Imperial Society of Teachers of Dancing (ISTD) Tap, Modern and Cecchetti Ballet and Rambert Grades Contemporary Dance.
Our dance pupils benefit from a dedicated studio and professional facilities, including a sprung floor in Roberts Hall, as well as access to the Ballroom and Theatre — all of which provide spaces to train, rehearse, and perform.

Misty Copeland
Art
In our dedicated School of Art and Design building pupils enjoy a broad curriculum that enables them to explore and develop a diverse range of skills, spanning painting, drawing, and sculpture to printmaking and working with clay.
Visiting artists are regularly invited to share unusual approaches and techniques. Pupils also benefit from visits to world leading London art galleries and museums as well as attending talks by internationally renowned contemporary artists such as Grayson Perry or Cornelia Parker. Art is ever popular at GCSE and A level, with impressive results at both levels.
